text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- ETA Basque separatists murder army officer hours after Herri Batasuna, ETA's political wing, declares "a future of suffering".
- Modern installation at Madrid's Barajas airport designed to remove ice on planes fails leaving airport in chaos.
EL MUNDO
- ETA woman shoots army officer in neck and her male companion finishes him off as he falls to ground.
DIARIO 16
- Policeman Jose Amedo says Spain's best known High Court judge Baltasar Garzon manipulated proceedings in various cases.
- ETA terror returns to Madrid.
ABC
- Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar succeeds in bringing unemployment to lowest level since 1982.
- ETA opens 1997 "negotiations" with murder of army officer.
CINCO DIAS
- Group of seven listed companies named the "billion club" control Spanish bourse.
- Tabacalera negotiates sale of Tabacos de Filipinas to U.S. group.
- Before talks on labour reforms between trade unions and businessmen begin, unions warn they want dismissal issues in pact while Jose Maria Cuevas wants change of law.
EXPANSION
- Markets expectations turn once again to cut in interest rates.
- Hilton buys Eurobuilding hotel.
- Trade unions demonstrate that they will not give in to demands of businessmen on labour reform.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Unemployment falls 14 percent for the first time in 15 years.
- Hilton launches takeover bid for Eurobuilding for 7 billion pesetas.
- Three banks which are key shareholders in Telefoncia have invested 300 billion pesetas to assure control of telecommunications group. mad mcm
